1433. 10. Jnli. 0. �?0. — Ulrich von Rosenberg verkauft dem Abte Sigismund und den Religiesen in Hohenfurt eilf Schock fünfzig Groschen zwei Pfenninge linse in dem Dorfe Hermannschlag um 118 Schock 24 Groschen und einen Pfenning Prager Münze.

CCXII. Pfenning Prager Münze. Nos Vlricus de Rosenberg tenore presenciu») vniuersis et sin- gulis profitemur, qui a sana cum deliberacione fidelium nostrorum consilio attendente vendidimus vndecim sexagenas grossorum quin- quaginta grossos duos denarios census annul in villa nostra Kurzim cum omni iurisdiccione, agris cultis et incultis censibus emendis honoranciis robotis pascuis pratis comunitatibus singulisque prouen- tibus iuribus et pertinenciis et pleno dominio et libertate, prout soli tenuimus, sic quod nee pro nobis aut nostris successoribus in eadem villa et eins incolis ¡am condescensis aliquid iuris reliquimus, sed in toto vendidimus wenerabili patri domino Sigismundo abbati et reli- giosis suis et fratribus monasterii nostri in Alionado vero et iusto vendicionis titulo pro centum decem et octo sexagenis viginti quatuor grossis minus vno denario monete Pragensis iure hereditario ad habcndum tenendum regendum possidendum vtifruendum libere et pacifice perpetuis temporibus, prout nosmet et antecessores nostri eandem villam hue usque libere et quiete dinoscimur tenuisse, et pro eadem willa Kurzim a prefatis abbate et conuentu monasterii nostri in Altouado recepimus omnes predictas peractas peccunias nos Vlri cus de Rosenberg antedictus. Eadem igitur bona nos Vlricus de Rosenbergh, Mathias Wissnye de Wietrznye, Chwal de Chmelni protunc castri Crupnaw purgrauius, et Petrus de Dluha protunc castri Welessin purgrauius, fideiussores pro et cum ipso domino Vlrico predicto de Rosenbergh omnes indiuisa manu fide nostra bona *) Diese eingeklammerte Stelle scheint von einer zweiten Hand geschrieben zu sein. 264 omni sine dolo volentes dictum abbatem eius et conuentum in huismodi (sic) empcione certos ac securos reddere promittimus, a data pre- sencium ad sex annos continue reuoluendos disbrigare et libertare ante omnes orphanos ante queuis dotalicia ante omnem hominem status cuiuslibet impetentem uel impetere volentem et fideliter ipsis sex annis expletis et decursis in primis quatuor temporibus tune venientibus aut finaliter in secundus quatuor temporibus proxime tune sequentibus prefatis abbati suis et fratribus conuentus mona- sterii nostri in Altouado intabulare ad terre tabulas regni Boemie bonos disbrigatores bonorum eorundem statuentes tune, veluti ius terre Boemie postulat et requirit. Si vero, quod absit, eandem vil- lam et bona cum omnibus appendiciis superius expressis disbrigare libertare aut intabulare negligeremus aut non possemus, extunc de tot et tantis et tam bonis nostris mundis et liberis propriis heredita- tibus, prout dicta bona se extendunt, eciam et tercia parte plus adaucta predictis abbati suis et fratribus condescendere promittimus et debemus, omni occasione et contradiccione procul motis. In casu autem, si nos in huiusmodi bonorum disbrigacione intabulacione aut aliorum in tercia parte plus valencium bonorum condescensione contrarii essemus et negligentes, extunc mox et statim duo nostrum, qui primum moniti fuerimus, se per alios non excusantes cum duobus fumulis et quatuor equis ingredi tenebimur ciuitatem Crumpnaw ad honestum ibidem hospitem, qui nobis per predictos deputatus fuerit, prestituri ibidem obstagium debitum et conswetum. Nos vero Vlricus de Rosenbérgh, si pro faciendo obstagio moniti fuerimus, tune loco nostri alium famosum clientem in ipsum obstagium poterimus collo- care, abinde nos obstagiantes, qui extiterimus, exituri nullo quo- quam super iure, nisi prius omnimode disbrigauerimus intabulaueri- mus bona eadem omnia supradicta, aut in bonis nostris tercia parte plus condescenderimus, veluti superius est expressum. Elapsis vero diebus quatuordecim a predicto obstagii termino continuis prestito per nos obstagio uel non prestito prefatis per nos nondum expletis predicti potestatem habent plenam, quam eis presenfibus damns et concedimus, predictas sortis peccunias cum tercia parte plus pec- cuniarum accrescente conquirendi nostrum omnium super dumpna inter Cristianos uel Judeos, nobis tamen semper tam diu dictum seruantibus obstagium, donee per nos prenominatis creditoribus nostris de predictis omnibus satisfactum fuerit plenarie et in toto, 265 eciam de dampnis omnibus et singulis , que predicti per legaciones itineraciones expensas inpensas seu per alium quemuis modum ob nostre negligencie incuriam perceperint et se ea percepisse iura- mento in cruce sine cespitacione, quod dicitur bez zmatku asserere presumpserint, satisfacere promittimus in toto, hoc eciam notanter expresso et excepto , quod nos Vlricus de Rosenbergh vna cum heredibus et successoribus nostris predictam villam Kur/.im, sicvt superius est tactum, per nos venditam ex speciali et beniuolo con- sonsu abbatis et conucntus monasterii nostri in Altouado, quando- cunque voluerimus, cum eadem summa peccuniarum, veluti est ven- dita, reemere possumus hominis cuiuslibet difficultate qualibet non obstante. Et si quis nostrum medio in tempore diuina permission« mortuus extiterit, vnus nut duo tune mox infra vnum mensem a die obitus illius uel ¡Jlornm continuum sub pena similis obstagii, ut pre- dicitur, eque probum uel probos habentem uel habentes nobiscum nos residui statuere spondemus loco defuncti uel defunctorum ad nos pro fideiussore assumentes litteram presentem infringendo et uliam de nono huic similem renouando, condicionibus tamen in ea verius obseruatis. Et si quis nostrum contra presentem literam se verbo uel facto opposuerit aut aliqua Juramenta prestare voluerit, hoc sit et esse debet in sui ipsius preiudicium, sed non huius litere detrimentum. Et quicunque presentem literam cum bona voluntate et pleno et libero consensu sepetactorum abbatis et conuentus monasterii nostri in Altouado babuerit, eidem ius conpetit omnium premissorum. In quorum omnium testimonium et firmius roboramen- Uim vt omnia premissa in singulis suis punctis et clausulis rata et firma permaneant, sigilla propria nostra de sciencia presentibus sunt appensa. Sub anno domini millesimo quadrigentesimo tricesimo tercio.feria sexta ante Margarethe. Vier, an Pergamentstrelfen hängende Siegel, das erste ¡n rothem, die übrigen in schwarzem Wachs. a) Das schon beschriebene Siegel Ulrich's von Rosenberg. b) Ein Schild mit sechs Bogen, deren Radien zu dritt nach oben und zu dritt nach unten stehen; darüber ein Helm, dessen Zierde ein Fässchen mit einem daraus entspringenden Baum (oder Federbusch?) ist. — S. Mathie. De. Wyetrznye. c) Ein Schild mit einer heraldischen Lilie, worüber ein Helm mit demselben Zeichen. — S . Chwalois . De . Chmelny. d) Ein Schild mit einem Hunde, worüber ein Helm mit auf den Hinterfüssen stehendem Hunde. — S . Petri , De . Longavia. Die letzten drei Siegel sind klein vun Gestalt. 266
entries.english:
1433, 10 July. Ulrich von Rosenberg sells to Abbot Sigismund and the religious of Hohenfurt an annual rent of eleven schock, fifty groschen, and two pennies in the village of Hermannschlag for 118 score, 24 groschen, and one Prague penny.

CCXII. Prague penny. We, Ulrich von Rosenberg, by the tenor of this present document, declare to all and each that, with sound deliberation and the counsel of our faithful men, we have sold eleven schock, fifty groschen, and two pennies of annual rent in our village of Kurzim, together with all jurisdiction, cultivated and uncultivated fields, rents, dues, services, pastures, meadows, commons, and every revenue, right, appurtenance, full lordship, and liberty, as we alone held them. Thus we have retained no right for ourselves or our successors in that village and its inhabitants, who have now been yielded up, but have sold it all to the venerable father Lord Sigismund, abbot, and his religious and brothers of our monastery at Altovado, by a true and lawful title of sale, for one hundred eighteen schock and twenty-four groschen less one penny of Prague currency, as an hereditary possession, to have, hold, govern, possess, use, and enjoy freely and peacefully for all time, just as we ourselves and our predecessors are known to have held that village freely and quietly until now. For that same village of Kurzim we, the aforesaid Ulrich von Rosenberg, have received from the aforesaid abbot and convent of our monastery at Altovado all the aforesaid payment in full.

Accordingly, we, Ulrich von Rosenberg, Matthias Wissnye von Wietrznye, Chwal von Chmelni, then burgrave of Crupnaw Castle, and Petrus von Dluha, then burgrave of Welessin Castle, as guarantors for and together with the said Lord Ulrich von Rosenberg, all with our joint pledge and good faith (the parenthesized passage appears to have been written by a second hand), wishing without deceit to make the said abbot and his convent secure in this purchase, promise to clear and warrant the property for six consecutive years from the date hereof, against all orphans, all dowries, and any person of any status who brings or wishes to bring a claim. When those six years have expired, during either the first four terms then falling due or, at the latest, the next four terms thereafter, we shall enter the said property for the abbot, his brothers, and the convent of our monastery at Altovado in the land registers of the Kingdom of Bohemia, appointing good warrantors for it as Bohemian land law requires. If, God forbid, we neglect or are unable to clear and warrant the said village and its property with all the appurtenances set out above, or to register it, then we promise and are bound to yield to the said abbot, his brothers, and the convent other clean and unencumbered hereditary properties of ours, equal to the value of the said property and increased by one third, all excuses and objections being set aside.

If, however, we were to resist or be negligent in clearing or registering the property, or in yielding other property worth one third more, then immediately two of us who are first summoned, without excusing themselves through the others, shall be bound to enter the city of Crumpnaw with two squires and four horses and there provide the customary surety-hostage at an honorable inn designated for us by those named above. If we, Ulrich von Rosenberg, are summoned to provide this hostage, we may put another reputable retainer in our place. Those of us who have given the hostage may not depart from there until we have fully cleared and registered all the property aforesaid, or yielded other property worth one third more, as stated above. If fourteen consecutive days have passed from the stated hostage term, whether or not we have provided the hostage, and the said obligations remain unfulfilled, the aforesaid creditors shall then have full power, which we grant them by this document, to recover from all of us the principal sums together with one third more, by recourse against Christians or Jews. We shall meanwhile keep the said hostage for as long as necessary, until we have fully satisfied our aforesaid creditors in all these matters. We also promise full compensation for every loss they have suffered through our negligence, whether from embassies, journeys, expenses and outlays, or in any other way, if they affirm on oath before the cross without hesitation that they have suffered it—the expression is “bez zmatku.”

It is also expressly stated and excepted that we, Ulrich von Rosenberg, together with our heirs and successors, may at any time, with the special and willing consent of the abbot and convent of our monastery at Altovado, buy back the said village of Kurzim sold by us as aforesaid, for the same sum of money for which it was sold, notwithstanding any difficulty raised by anyone. If, by divine permission, any of us should die in the meantime, we who remain promise, within one month continuously from the day of his or their death, under the same penalty of hostage as aforesaid, to appoint in place of the deceased one or two men of equally good standing, who have as many squires or more, taking them as guarantors for ourselves; we shall cancel this letter and renew another like it, while more faithfully observing its conditions. If any of us should oppose this present letter by word or deed, or wish to take any oath, that shall be to his own prejudice and not to the detriment of this letter. Whoever holds this letter with the good will and full and free consent of the aforesaid abbot and convent of our monastery at Altovado shall have the right to all the foregoing. In testimony and firmer confirmation of all this, that each point and clause may remain valid and firm, our own seals have been knowingly appended to this document. In the year of the Lord 1433, on the Friday before Margaret’s feast.

Four seals hang from parchment strips, the first in red wax and the others in black wax. (a) The previously described seal of Ulrich von Rosenberg. (b) A shield with six arcs, their radii arranged three upward and three downward; above it a helmet whose crest is a small barrel with a tree (or plume?) growing out of it. Seal of Matthias von Wietrznye. (c) A shield with a heraldic lily, above it a helmet bearing the same device. Seal of Chwal von Chmelny. (d) A shield with a dog, above it a helmet bearing a dog standing on its hind legs. Seal of Petrus von Longavia. The last three seals are small.
